dct_description_sm: The general goal of the FreshwaterMarine Interactions Project is to document and study transfers of freshwater, suspended sediments, nutrients and organic matter into Hudson Bay from its watershed, to trace their circulation through Hudson Bay and, in particular, to investigate their effect on the light regime in Hudson Bay, with emphasis on studies in and near the estuaries of the Churchill and Hayes  Nelson Rivers in the southwest, and the Rivire de la Grande Baleine in the southeast.  The particular goals of this mission were twofold:  1)  a collaborative systematic study on the relationship of water masses to organic matter composition (DOC) and the carbonate system, using tracers, including salinity, CDOM & FDOM, δ18O) and alkalinity to determine the key drivers of carbon fluxes in Hudson Bay; and 2) a survey of dimensions and gradients (salinity, SPM, chl-a, DOC, CDOM, major nutrients, δ18O) of the plume of the Hayes and Nelson Rivers in Hudson Bay.    The collaborative study involves researchers from several institutions:  1) G. McCullough (Principal Investigator D. Barber, U. Manitoba, Winnipeg, MB)  freshwater-marine interactions and remote sensing; 2) T. Papakyriakou (U. Manitoba, Winnipeg, MB)  carbon fluxes; 3) R. Macdonald (IOS, Sydney, BC) and M. Granskog (Norwegian Polar Institute, Troms, Norway)  freshwater circulation; and 4) L. Miller and S. Johannesson (IOS, Sydney, BC) and T. Helmuth (Dalhousie U., Halifax, NS)  DIC, TA, photochemical processes.  This dataset includes only the data collected by Barber/McCullough.  Contact collaborators to determine availability of associated data sets.
